newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares lose 1.33 pct in correction.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares lose 1.33 pct in correction.

text.p: Istanbul shares lost an average 1.33 percent on Wednesday in profit-taking that followed the recent sharp gains fuelled by political optimism, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 27 points, or 1.33 percent, lower at 2,009, bringing the fall to 1.7 percent since Monday's all-time high close of 2,043. The index brushed a low of 1,972 in the afternoon when sales accelerated.

Daily trade volume dropped to 24.06 trillion lira, down 15 percent from Tuesday's 28.26 trillion. Separately, a 4.2 trillion lira block sale of Sabanci Holding shares to investors abroad were made on the wholesale market.
Brokers said the correction was an expected development after the recent gains.
The market index had soared 30.5 percent to Monday's all-time closing high of 2,043 amid hopes for the new government following the June 18 resignation of the former Islamist-led government.
The new right-left coalition government won a key confidence vote in parliament on Saturday, ending driving expectations in the market.
"Shares of state and energy firms were selectively sold in the afternoon because they were the ones that posted the biggest premiums during the rally," said Guzin Ozdemir from Ata Securities.

"The index rebounded from 1,970 today so I don't expect this support to be breaken on thursday. I suggest investors to keep their stocks having bright six-month profit prospects because the index may still have some more room to go (up) until August," she added.

Of the 246 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 145 to 48 and 53 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial dropped 1.23 percent to 1,925, the IMKB Services dived 1.99 percent to 1,916 and the IMKB Financial lost 1.46 percent to 2,159.
The index representing the tourism sector was the leading loser with a 3.62 percent fall while the insurance sector was the top gainer with a 3.11 percent premium.

Leading actives were Akbank, a leading commercial bank, down 750 lira at 10,000, glass maker Anadolu Cam, up 175 lira at 2,525 and largely state-owned flat steel maker Eregli, down 500 lira at 26,000. They made up 16.4 percent of the total turnover.
